correctness.rationale: Uniform type-A noncrossing partition root-block decomposition and Lagrange inversion yield M_n(gamma)=(n+1)_[t]/((n+1)C_n) * binom(2n-t-w,n-w), w=sum(r gamma_r) and t=sum gamma_r, for w<=n, zero otherwise. For residual weak compositions into m=n+1-t>=N+1=n-w+1 cells, the two-mark factorial ratio is nonincreasing in each positive block size r,s. At r=s=1 its denominator minus numerator is 4N(N-1)(N-2)+(4N^2-7N+1)h+(3N-2)h^2+h^3 >=0, h=m-N-1; equality only residual N=2,m=3,r=s=1. Chaining local ratios proves strict all-order product inequalities for disjoint supports because the initial n>=3 is not exceptional; infeasible combined total has zero moment. At n=3 direct noncrossing partition enumeration gives Cov(X1,X2)=-3/25 while Cov(1_[X1>=1],1_[X2>=1])=+3/25, excluding ordinary negative association. The actual source verify.py enumerates noncrossing partitions and exact moments at bounded n; the finite checks are corroboration, not a proof of all n.

value.rationale: Block-size multiplicities are canonical statistics of noncrossing partitions. A strict arbitrary-order finite factorial repulsion bound controls simultaneous block-size occurrence even for rare sizes where fixed-size asymptotics do not apply. Its positive n=3 increasing-event covariance sharply demonstrates the limitation of the dependence notion, a substantive boundary rather than a routine restatement of known Catalan coefficients.
residual_risks: Value concerns factorial dependence, not generalized association, regression, arbitrary partitions, or a causal model.

limitations: Uniform classical noncrossing partitions only; n>=3 strict inequality; all marked sizes positive, integer orders, disjoint supports.
Does not imply negative association of arbitrary increasing functions; no general Coxeter type theorem.
